title: Coconut-flour tortillas
summary: Pliable, grain-free tortillas from coconut flour and psyllium, cooked in a dry skillet for tacos or wraps.
steps: Whisk the coconut flour, psyllium, salt and baking powder.
Add the hot water and olive oil and stir, then knead for a minute into a smooth, slightly tacky dough. Rest 10 minutes.
Divide into 8 balls. Roll each between two sheets of parchment into a thin round about 15 cm (6 in) across; a tortilla press also works.
Heat a dry cast-iron or non-stick pan over medium-high heat. Cook each tortilla 1–1½ minutes per side, until spotted brown.
Stack under a clean towel as they come off the pan; the steam keeps them soft.
tips: If the dough cracks when rolled, knead in another tablespoon of hot water.
Coconut flour varies in how much water it absorbs; adjust by the spoonful.

origin.history: Tortillas are an ancient Mesoamerican food, made from maize cooked with lime (nixtamalised) and ground into masa, then cooked on a clay griddle called a comal. Wheat-flour tortillas came later, after the Spanish brought wheat. This version is a modern low-carb stand-in that uses neither.
